candidates.claim: After switching Accept to application/octet-stream, getSecretPayload still reads the body with res.text(). For binary secrets (e.g. application/octet-stream keys, PKCS12 certificates) the bytes are decoded as UTF-8, so Reveal Payload and Copy show corrupted data (replacement characters). Text payloads are unaffected.
candidates.evidence: keyManagerRouter.ts lines 100-111 at 64c47a9: request with Accept: application/octet-stream, then `const text = await res.text()` and `return { payload: text, contentType }`. The delta does not touch the read path or base64-encode non-text content types.
candidates.precedent: The raw-text read was already there before this commit; the Accept change is what makes binary bodies reachable.

candidates.claim: The Key Manager canUser router only reports policy decisions. None of the tRPC procedures (getSecretPayload, deleteSecret, deleteContainer, deleteOrder, create*, update*) checks the policy before calling Barbican. A caller can use the tRPC API directly to run an action the UI hides and Aurora's policy denies, whenever Barbican itself allows it. This includes revealing secret payloads, since the hidden control is only a client-side gate.
candidates.evidence: At the head commit, keyManagerRouter.ts procedures use projectScopedProcedure and go straight to km.get/post/del with no policy check (e.g. getSecretPayload lines 93-112, deleteSecret 153-162). The permission router is only spread in at index.ts:7-8. The only server-side policy code is in the permissionRouter.ts files and createPermissionRouter.ts, so nothing enforces a decision. The delta did not add a guard.
candidates.precedent: Compute, Network and Storage routers do not enforce policy server-side either. Only their permissionRouter.ts files and createPermissionRouter.ts use the engine, so the pattern is accepted elsewhere.
candidates.discussion: Raised by Copilot in https://github.com/cobaltcore-dev/aurora-dashboard/pull/1393#discussion_r4360389025 (CRITICAL, unanswered). Still applies at 64c47a99. Other Copilot threads were checked at head and look addressed: Accept header and debug:false on payload (keyManagerRouter.ts:98-104), isEnabled on the nav entry (buildNavSections.ts:154), nullable secret_refs name (keyManager.ts:25), canDelete renamed to canDeleteContainer/Secret/Order, hook renamed to useKeyManagerPermissions, payload gating via canRevealPayload (SecretDetailsView.tsx:21-22), bit length validation (OrderModals.tsx:42-46), menu toggle label and separator, and page step-back on an empty page (SecretsList.tsx:70-75). The container-secret DELETE endpoint no longer exists in the router.

candidates.claim: getSecretPayload hardcodes Accept: application/octet-stream. Barbican requires the Accept header on /payload to be one of the values in the secret's content_types, so a secret stored with another type (for example text/plain) can get 406 Not Acceptable. mapKmError turns that into INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, and the user sees 'Key Manager get secret payload failed' when revealing the payload. It works only for secrets whose content type is application/octet-stream.
candidates.evidence: Code at 64c47a99, keyManagerRouter.ts:100-104: `.get(`v1/secrets/${encodeURIComponent(input.secretId)}/payload`, { headers: { Accept: "application/octet-stream" }, debug: false })`. Reference (barbican doc/source/api/reference/secrets.rst, raw github, section 'GET /v1/secrets/{uuid}/payload', rendered at https://docs.openstack.org/barbican/latest/api/reference/secrets.html#get-secrets-uuid-payload): "When making a request for a secret's payload, you must set the accept header to one of the values listed in the ``content_types`` attribute of a secret's metadata." The documented example sends `Accept: text/plain`, and the status table lists `406 | Not Acceptable`. The secret metadata example shows `"content_types": {"default": "application/octet-stream"}` for opaque secrets only. The client already reads secret.content_types (SecretDetailsView.tsx:51), so the server could use content_types.default or fetch the secret first. Barbican source barbican/api/controllers/secrets.py: when there is no Accept header it defaults to 'application/octet-stream', otherwise it uses the header value. In signal-openstack at 64c47a99, grep for 'accept' in packages/signal-openstack/src finds nothing, so the in-code comment claiming a default 'Accept: application/json' is not backed by that client. I could not check what undici/fetch sends by default. Secondary: the body is read with res.text() (line 110), which corrupts binary payloads.
candidates.precedent: Other KM calls (getSecret, listSecrets) send no Accept header; the docs show Accept: application/json on those metadata calls.

candidates.claim: The container secret reference schema was loosened to name nullable, but the Barbican docs only show named references; the docs do not say a null name is allowed. The new test comment 'Barbican allows unnamed references' has no support in the container reference. The docs say a generic container's reference name is not restricted ('no specific restrictions are enforced on the contents name attribute'), but they do not document null.
candidates.evidence: Code: `secret_refs: z.array(z.object({ name: z.string().nullable(), secret_ref: z.string() }))`. Reference (barbican doc/source/api/reference/containers.rst, https://docs.openstack.org/barbican/latest/api/reference/containers.html): 'This type of container holds any number of references to secrets. Each secret reference is accompanied by a name. Unlike other container types, no specific restrictions are enforced on the contents name attribute.' All response examples show `"name": "private_key"`. I found no doc text saying name may be null. Low severity: the lenient schema is safe at runtime, but the claim in the test title is unverified. I did not check the Barbican source for null names.

candidates.claim: The new payload gating (key-manager:secrets:payload via canUser) is client-only. The getSecretPayload procedure is a plain projectScopedProcedure with no server-side canUser/policy check, so anyone calling the tRPC endpoint directly skips the UI gate; only Barbican's own policy then decides. Same holds for the delete/create procedures whose buttons are now hidden by canUser.
candidates.evidence: keyManagerRouter.ts:93-111 getSecretPayload: projectScopedProcedure, input schema, then a km.get of the payload path with no canUser/policy evaluation. The delta (SecretDetailsView.tsx) hides the Reveal Payload UI behind useKeyManagerPermissions only. The policy rule key-manager:secrets:payload exists in apps/dashboard/src/policies/key-manager.json:12 (rule:context_is_keymanager_viewer) and packages/aurora/src/server/KeyManager/routers/permissionRouter.ts:6, but is used only by the canUser query. Barbican enforces its own RBAC with the rescoped token, so this is defense-in-depth rather than a direct bypass. The handler code predates the delta; the delta adds only the client gate and debug:false.
candidates.precedent: Other domains (Compute/Network/Storage) also gate mainly in the UI via canUser; not checked whether any enforces it server-side in mutations.
